concept.prompt:
Use case: historical-scene.
Asset type: visual development reference for an existing modest low-poly Three.js first-person web game; NOT a photograph, NOT a cinematic, NOT an asset sheet.
Input images: the three supplied black-and-white archival reproductions are reference images ONLY for building silhouette, timber watchtower construction and wire fencing. Their dates are uncertain. Do not reproduce the photos, museum exhibits or printed layout.
Create one coherent player-eye-height 1.78m perspective of the Crveni Krst camp inspired level near Nis in February 1942, at winter night, deliberately modest game geometry and restrained realistic pixel-textured materials. Important recognizable long MASONRY storehouse with ground floor, first floor and low hipped tile roof, regular tall windows, faint facade pilasters, chimneys, based on references. NOT a camp of timber prisoner barracks. A small timber observation tower with square railed platform, cross-braced supports, hip roof and one utilitarian searchlight. Foreground intersection of narrow traversable outdoor paths: aged timber posts and readable horizontal/diagonal barbed wire, a solid timber privacy screen hiding one branch, open snowy yard glimpsed between them. One standard-size German guard distant for scale, not hero portrait. Snow lying on ground and roof edges, trodden darker earth along paths, very sparse bare winter vegetation, rural-town outskirts with no modern buildings.
Composition must show a believable traversable junction, visible alternate route round building, foreground and midground at same human scale, building and tower orient player beyond the maze. Fences are visibly porous; screen and masonry are visibly opaque. Use two understandable localized warm lamps against cool muted blue-grey night; enough fill to read textures, no pitch black. A restrained searchlight pool, no cinematic fog beams. Horizontal landscape frame 1536x1024 if available.
All objects grounded, consistent perspective, quiet flat ambient texture lighting with localized actual game lights. No huge fortress, no concrete wall maze, no razor ribbon coils, no modern mesh fence, no flag graphics, no slogans, no HUD, no text, no gore. This is an interpretive gameplay composition, NOT an asserted historical site plan.
concept.status: Visual direction, not a rendered game screenshot or measured reconstruction

atlas.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one actual production diffuse texture atlas for original low-poly 3D web-game camp buildings, 1024 by 1024 square pixels. This is a flat MATERIAL TEXTURE SHEET, not a scene, not a model preview, not an infographic.
An exact edge-to-edge two-by-two grid of four square flat surfaces of exactly equal size, touching without margins, titles or borders. Every quadrant fills exactly 50% width and 50% height.
TOP LEFT QUADRANT: aged pale warm grey-beige lime plaster, subtle trowel grain and faint hairline cracks, faint dirt speckling, restrained low contrast, absolutely no huge damaged patches or exposed brick or windows.
TOP RIGHT QUADRANT: weathered dull clay roof tiles, small regular horizontal rows of overlapping dark desaturated brown terracotta tiles, viewed straight perpendicular to roof plane, quiet narrow creases and highlights, no perspective.
BOTTOM LEFT QUADRANT: old untreated dark grey-brown sawn timber planks, grain aligned vertically, subtle knots and narrow plank seams, desaturated, low-contrast, no text, no nails or metal hardware.
BOTTOM RIGHT QUADRANT: dark oxidized brown-grey steel with sparse fine pitting, subtle edge-free mottling, no screws, no painted markings, no highlights.
Style: restrained realistic hand-authored pixel textures suitable for a serious retro Three.js war game; visible small clustered pixels at native size, no painterly streaks, no photoreal high-frequency grit, no black outlining, no cartoon. Same quiet grey-beige/brown palette and texel detail across all four panels.
Lighting is unlit flat diffuse albedo, neutral even light, no cast shadows, no vignette, no illumination gradient, no ambient occlusion or sun glare. No props, buildings, people, signs, lettering, frames, guides, labels, watermark. Tileable feeling within each quadrant, grain and roof pattern meet opposite edges as closely as possible.
atlas.layout: Top-left plaster, top-right roof, bottom-left timber, bottom-right steel. Original generated image retained without visual edits; actual dimensions recorded by build.py.
